page: Amazon Web Services m6a.8xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by third-generation AMD EPYC 7R13 processors. Featuring an x86_64 architecture, this instance supplies 32 virtual CPUs derived from 16 dedicated physical cores running at clock speeds up to 3.6 GHz. It provides 128 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, preserving a standard 1:4 core-to-memory allocation of 4 GB RAM per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated hardware accelerators or bundled local NVMe storage, relying entirely on network-attached storage while maintaining a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps.

Benchmark results highlight strong single-thread throughput and memory subsystem responsiveness. The m6a.8xlarge achieved top-quartile results in stress-ng single-core processing and PassMark memory evaluations, complemented by high cryptographic performance via hardware-accelerated AES and SHA-NI instruction sets. Multi-core execution across general workloads, including PassMark CPU tests, Geekbench multi-core runs, and Redis SET operations (35.1 million operations per second), sits firmly within the middle 50th percentile. For machine learning tasks, lightweight inference on small models performs strongly, whereas large-parameter models demonstrate low throughput, reflecting the absence of specialized accelerators and AVX-512 instructions.

The instance balances compute capacity and RAM density, making it a cost-efficient deployment target for general enterprise applications. The trade-off lies in the omission of local instance storage and advanced vector extensions such as AVX-512 and AMX, which limits its suitability for deep matrix operations or ultra-low-latency scratch storage. It is best suited for production relational databases, distributed caching nodes, CI/CD compilation pipelines, mid-tier application runtimes, and static web serving workloads requiring predictable multi-threaded CPU and memory resources.
description: Amazon Web Services m6a.8xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the AWS Nitro System, driven by a 32-vCPU AMD EPYC 7R13 processor operating at up to 3.6 GHz across 16 physical cores. The instance features 128 GB of DDR4 system memory at a consistent 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, alongside a 12 Gbps baseline network link. The configuration does not include local storage or dedicated GPU acceleration, relying on remote block storage for persistent data. Performance evaluations demonstrate strong single-thread processing, memory bandwidth efficiency, and cryptographic throughput, with balanced mid-tier results in multi-core metrics and static web serving. Due to the lack of AVX-512 extensions and local high-speed disks, heavy vector computation and I/O-intensive scratch workloads face constraints. The instance is well matched for enterprise web serving, compilation pipelines, relational database tiers, and microservices.
